shell_window_error: The window action failed. Please try again.
shell_update_unsupported: {version} is available. This install cannot update itself.
shell_update_dialog_body: Filtering pauses for a few seconds while the daemon restarts. Antiwire must be reopened afterwards to finish the update.
onboarding_step_retention_title: Choose how long logs are kept
onboarding_welcome_body: Antiwire is a cross-platform security and privacy monitor for your computer. It helps you understand what is connecting, protect your DNS, block unwanted destinations, and investigate network activity from one local dashboard.
onboarding_welcome_see_body: Follow live traffic, applications, connections, and daily activity.
onboarding_welcome_control_body: Use encrypted DNS, blocklists, and firewall rules to shape what gets through.
onboarding_welcome_local_body: Your monitoring data and preferences stay on this device.
onboarding_welcome_note: Choose your preferences next. You can change them later in Settings.
onboarding_waiting_daemon_body: Setup will continue automatically as soon as the desktop service connects.
onboarding_resolver_body: Encrypt DNS lookups so other devices on the path cannot easily read them.
onboarding_protocol_doh_detail: Encrypts DNS inside normal HTTPS traffic. It works with the widest choice of providers.
onboarding_protocol_doh3_detail: Carries DNS over HTTPS on HTTP/3 and QUIC for faster connections. It stops working on networks that block QUIC.
onboarding_protocol_dot_detail: Uses a dedicated encrypted DNS connection. It is easy to understand, but easier for a network to identify or block.
onboarding_protocol_doq_detail: Uses modern QUIC transport for quick reconnects and better loss handling. Fewer public providers support DoQ.
onboarding_blocklists_lead: Blocklists stop known advertising, tracking, and malicious domains before a connection is made.
onboarding_geoip_body: Add country and region context to remote IP addresses in records and analytics.
onboarding_geoip_privacy_note: The location database runs locally. It does not share your traffic with a GeoIP service.
onboarding_desktop_notifications_body: Show Alerts events through your operating system.
onboarding_desktop_notifications_note: Events still appear on the Alerts page when this is off.
onboarding_alert_new_connections_body: When a new outbound destination is observed.
onboarding_alert_new_apps_body: When an unknown program first accesses the network.
onboarding_alert_threats_body: High-severity blocks and threat intelligence matches.
onboarding_retention_lead: Connection records help explain what happened. Choose how long Antiwire should retain them on this computer.
onboarding_retention_note: Unlimited keeps records until you clear them manually. Blocklists and firewall rules are not affected.
onboarding_toast_complete_body: Your privacy preferences are now active.
onboarding_error_daemon_rejected: The daemon did not accept the setup settings.
settings_updates_intro: Choose which releases Antiwire offers you, and check for a new one.
settings_updates_channel_desc: How early you get new versions. Each channel also gets the releases of the more stable ones.
settings_updates_channel_stable_desc: Tested releases. Recommended for most people.
settings_updates_channel_beta_desc: Previews of the next release, to try new features early.
settings_updates_channel_nightly_desc: Development builds of the newest code, published by the developers. Expect rough edges.
settings_updates_checking_body: Reading the release lists from GitHub.
settings_updates_never_checked_body: Antiwire checks every few hours. You can also check now.
settings_updates_up_to_date_body: {version} is the newest release your channel offers.
settings_updates_available_body: You have {current}. Filtering pauses for a few seconds while the service restarts.
settings_updates_unsupported: This copy of Antiwire can't install updates
settings_updates_switch_stay_body: Antiwire never installs an older version, so this channel reaches you with its first release newer than yours.
settings_updates_switch_now: After you switch, Antiwire checks this channel right away and offers its newest release.
settings_ai_intro: TypeSafe scores each domain. You choose how sure a score must be, and whether Antiwire blocks on that score or only reports it.
settings_ai_enable_desc: Ask TypeSafe about advertising, tracking, telemetry, analytics, malware, lookalike fraud, cryptomining, and tunnels.
settings_ai_key_desc: Stored encrypted in the daemon database and kept in zeroizing memory while Antiwire is running.
settings_secret_saved_placeholder: Saved. Enter a new value to replace it.
settings_secret_cleared_placeholder: Will be removed when you save.
settings_ai_mode_proactive_desc: Wait for the score before returning an address, so the first lookup for a domain is slower. A category set to Block stops that lookup when the score meets its minimum, and no address is returned. If the score is not ready in time, the lookup is allowed and the result is saved for the next one. Categories set to Record are saved and never block.
settings_ai_mode_retroactive_desc: Answer every lookup immediately, then score the domain in the background. The first lookup is always allowed. A later lookup for that same domain is blocked when a saved score meets a category set to Block. Categories set to Record are saved and never block.
settings_ai_types_desc: Turn each category on or off, and choose whether a match is blocked or only recorded.
settings_ai_confidence_desc: Minimum score, from 60 to 100, before that category counts. A higher minimum matches fewer domains.
settings_empty_daemon_cannot_load: Daemon not connected — settings cannot be loaded.
settings_toast_not_applied_title: Saved, but not all settings took effect
settings_language_desc: Choose the display language for the desktop client.
settings_theme_desc: Use a light or dark interface, or follow the operating system.
settings_desktop_notifications_desc: Show alerts as native operating-system notifications.
settings_new_connection_alerts_desc: Notify when a new outbound connection is observed.
settings_new_application_alerts_desc: Prompt when an unknown binary requests network access.
settings_threat_alerts_desc: Surface high-severity events in the alert feed.
settings_geoip_desc: Attach country codes to connection records.
settings_persist_rules_desc: Keep firewall rules when the daemon disconnects.
settings_save_lookups_desc: Store the official registration record when you run an advanced check.
settings_log_retention_desc: Retain connection logs and weekly activity history for configured period.
settings_database_size_desc: Disk space the stored connection history takes on this device.
settings_accent_desc: Primary and secondary highlights update together across the app.
settings_doh_blocking_desc: Block known DoH providers to prevent DNS bypass.
settings_group_private_relay_desc: macOS turns Private Relay off while an app filters packets, as Antiwire does.
settings_private_relay_desc: Antiwire stops using the macOS packet filter, so Private Relay can stay on. Domain rules and blocklists still apply to lookups made through the system's DNS settings.
settings_private_relay_warning: Largely untested, and it can weaken blocking. Rules on addresses, applications and countries are switched off, as are DNS-over-HTTPS blocking and the redirect of apps that use their own DNS server. Traffic that Private Relay carries is not filtered.
settings_dns_provider_hint_doq: Only providers with a public DoQ endpoint are shown.
settings_dns_provider_hint_default: Select the upstream DNS service to use.
settings_blocklists_desc: Sync blocklist for blocking ads, malware, analytics, etc.
settings_blocklist_dialog_intro: Select community blocklists to enable. Lists sync automatically based on your update frequency.
settings_blocklist_group_hagezi_hint: Higher levels block more and break more sites. One is usually enough.
settings_blocklist_hagezi_multi_desc: Balanced protection, recommended for most users.
settings_blocklist_hagezi_pro_desc: Aggressive protection, may cause minor breakage.
settings_blocklist_hagezi_pro_mini_desc: (Smaller) Aggressive protection, may cause minor breakage.
settings_blocklist_hagezi_pro_plus_plus_: More aggressive protection, may cause minor breakage.
(Smaller) More Aggressive protection, may cause minor breakage.
settings_blocklist_hagezi_ultimate_desc: Very aggressive protection, will cause breakage.
settings_blocklist_hagezi_ultimate_mini_: (Smaller) Very aggressive protection, will cause breakage.
settings_blocklist_hagezi_tif_desc: Threat intelligence feeds only, no ad blocking.
settings_blocklist_urlhaus_desc: Malware sites from abuse.ch, with popular domains left out.
settings_blocklist_phishing_army_desc: Known phishing domains, updated every few hours.
settings_blocklist_stevenblack_desc: Classic unified hosts file with adware and malware.
settings_blocklist_hagezi_tlds_desc: HaGeZi's conservative abused-TLD list, plus .christmas, .zip, and .mov. Avoids everyday consumer TLDs, but can still block real sites on those namespaces.
settings_abused_tlds_desc: Sinkhole HaGeZi's most-abused top-level domains, plus .christmas, .zip, and .mov. This can break real sites on those namespaces.
settings_group_new_domains_desc: Scam and malware sites often use domains that are only days old.
settings_new_domains_desc: Ask each domain's official registry when it was registered and block domains younger than the age below. Domains whose date can't be found are allowed.
settings_group_details_desc: Extra information saved with each record.
settings_group_rules_desc: How your rules behave while the daemon is disconnected.
settings_group_history_desc: How long connection records and activity stay on this device.
settings_group_delete_history_desc: Remove connection records, the activity they add to the dashboard, and alerts from this device.
settings_delete_recent_desc: Everything recorded in the chosen period, up to now.
settings_delete_all_desc: Every connection record, all activity and every alert.
settings_delete_history_amount_invalid: Enter a whole number from 1 to {max}.
settings_delete_recent_dialog_body: Connection records, activity and alerts from {start} until now will be permanently deleted.
settings_delete_all_dialog_body: All connection records, activity and alerts will be permanently deleted.
settings_delete_history_dialog_kept: Rules, settings and applications are kept. Connections that are still open are recorded again from now on.
settings_group_resolver_desc: Where this device's DNS queries go, and how they are protected.
settings_group_classification_desc: Score domains with TypeSafe and decide when a score counts.
settings_group_discovery_desc: Find devices on your local network automatically.
settings_group_destinations_desc: Where events are sent. Turn on any combination.
settings_group_event_types_desc: Choose which events leave this device.
settings_power_user_enable_desc: Unlock advanced DNS controls. These options can break connectivity if misconfigured.
settings_dns_rebinding_desc: Block responses that resolve to local addresses.
settings_dns_local_names_desc: Keep .local names off upstream DNS. Turn off if your network's internal domain ends in .local, such as an Active Directory domain.
settings_power_user_dialog_intro: This section is intended for power users and advanced network configurations.
settings_power_user_dialog_callout: These settings may cause issues with internet connectivity and reliability. They can also break apps that rely on private-address DNS answers or non-standard resolver behavior.
settings_power_user_dialog_footnote: Only enable this if you understand the impact.
settings_network_auto_scan_desc: Periodically discover devices on configured ranges.
settings_siem_enable_desc: Send security events to file, syslog, and/or HTTP webhook sinks.
settings_siem_file_desc: Append JSON events for a Wazuh agent localfile (or similar).
settings_siem_syslog_desc: Forward events to a remote syslog receiver (Wazuh manager or other).
settings_siem_webhook_desc: POST JSON events to an HTTP(S) endpoint.
settings_about_tagline: Open-source network monitor and firewall client for the Antiwire daemon.
settings_about_description: Built for highly secure environments. The desktop client runs with standard user privileges and talks to the elevated Antiwire service daemon over a pinned gRPC channel.
settings_about_license_intro: Antiwire is free and open source. You may use, modify, and redistribute it under the terms below. The copyright notice and permission notice must be retained in all copies or substantial portions.
settings_about_frameworks_intro: Antiwire is built on open platforms. Their license notices apply to the redistributed runtime components.
settings_about_packages_intro: Direct npm dependencies used by this desktop client. Transitive packages inherit their own licenses from npm.
settings_about_fonts_intro: Font Software redistributed or fetched for the UI must retain copyright and license notices (SIL OFL for IBM Plex Sans and JetBrains Mono).
settings_about_data_intro: Optional and embedded data sources. CC BY and project licenses require attribution when those features are used.
settings_about_runtime_intro: Native drivers and libraries that may be required on the host system and are not bundled as npm packages.
settings_about_legal_footer: Antiwire is provided as-is under the MIT License. Third-party components remain the property of their respective owners and are used under their own license terms. This notice is for attribution and compliance; it does not grant additional rights beyond those licenses. Full package license texts ship with the corresponding source distributions on npm and in the React / Electron SDKs.
settings_about_role_system_mono: Preferred system monospace on Windows when installed
settings_about_role_windivert: Windows flow ownership and DNS packet diversion (runtime)
settings_about_role_libpcap: Packet capture on macOS / Linux (planned platforms)

firewall_empty_disconnected: Daemon not connected — rules and applications unavailable.
firewall_apps_hint: Applications appear here the first time they open a connection.
firewall_empty_no_apps_with_path: No applications with a known executable path yet.
firewall_empty_no_allowed_apps: No allowed applications match the current filter.
firewall_empty_no_blocked_apps: No blocked applications match the current filter.
firewall_add_target_body: Choose a rule type, then enter a target or pick a country to block or allow matching traffic.
firewall_add_target_no_cidrs: No IPv4 CIDR blocks found for {code}.
firewall_add_target_load_cidrs_failed: Could not load CIDR blocks for {code}.
firewall_add_target_cidrs_hint: {count} IPv4 CIDR {blockWord} will be added for {country}.
firewall_add_app_body: Browse for an executable, or pick a recent application that is not already listed on the Applications tab.
firewall_add_app_browse_unavailable_titl: File browse is available in the desktop app
firewall_add_app_no_match: No other application matches your search.
firewall_add_app_already_listed_hint: Applications already on the Applications tab are managed from their cards.
firewall_remove_rule_body: This will remove the rule for {target}. Matching traffic will no longer be affected by this rule.
firewall_remove_country_body: This will remove the country block for {label}.
firewall_remove_country_networks_affecte: {count} network ranges will no longer be affected by this rule.
firewall_remove_country_matching_affecte: Matching traffic will no longer be affected by this rule.
records_empty_disconnected: Daemon not connected — connect to view live sockets.
records_apps_none_live: No applications are connected right now.
records_empty_no_sockets: No sockets match the current filters.
records_lookup_hint: Reads {domain}'s official record from its registry. Only the domain name is sent.
records_lookup_no_domain: Registration lookups need a domain name, and this record only has an IP address.
records_lookup_not_found: The registry has no registration for {domain}.
records_lookup_rate_limited: The registry is limiting requests. Try again in a minute.
records_lookup_no_authority: IANA lists no lookup service for this domain ending.
records_lookup_unavailable: The registry could not be reached or sent an unreadable record.
records_lookup_invalid_domain: This record does not name a domain that can be looked up.
records_lookup_not_public: {domain} is not a public domain name, so no registry holds it.
records_lookup_inferred: This name was inferred from DNS traffic rather than seen requested, so the connection may have gone to a different site.
records_dns_refresh_aria: Look up the DNS records again
records_dns_hint: Asks your DNS provider directly for the current records of {host} and its domain. Antiwire's filtering does not change the answers, and your provider sees these queries.
records_dns_no_mail: No mail records, so {domain} does not receive email.
records_subdomains_refresh_aria: Show the names seen here again
records_subdomains_local_hint: Names under this domain that apps on this device connected to or looked up. Finding the domain may ask your DNS provider for this host's zone.
records_subdomains_local_empty: Nothing under {domain} has been seen on this device yet.
records_subdomains_ct_hint: Lists every name on a public TLS certificate for {domain}, expired ones included. This sends {domain} to crt.sh, a third-party service run by Sectigo, and can take up to a minute.
records_subdomains_ct_loading: Searching certificate logs… this can take a minute.
records_subdomains_ct_truncated: crt.sh returned more than Antiwire reads, so the list is partial.
records_subdomains_ct_rate_limited: crt.sh is limiting requests. Try again in a few minutes.
records_subdomains_ct_unavailable: crt.sh did not answer. It is often slow for large domains; try again later.
capture_offline_body: Connect to the local Antiwire daemon to record a bounded packet capture. Capture data stays on this device and is never sent to a remote service.
capture_provider_unavailable_fallback: Install Npcap on Windows or libpcap on macOS/Linux, then restart the daemon.
capture_bars_packets_aria: Packets per sample, most recent last
capture_bars_bytes_aria: Capture rate per sample, most recent last
capture_app_help: Keeps only this application's TCP and UDP traffic on the selected interface. Lookups the system resolver makes on its behalf are not included.
capture_app_unavailable: Application capture needs connection attribution, which the daemon cannot provide right now.
capture_storage_help: Capture bytes are staged in a private local temporary file until the session is replaced or the daemon exits.
capture_promiscuous_desc: Include packets not addressed to this host.
capture_chart_empty_body: Start a capture to watch packet volume in real time.
capture_packet_empty: Packets appear here as the daemon captures them. Select a row to open its metadata and captured bytes in the packet inspector.
capture_sample_empty: Counter samples appear here once a capture starts. These are daemon-reported totals, not synthetic packet rows.
capture_status_install_provider: Install a packet capture provider, then restart the daemon.
capture_status_could_not_start: The daemon could not start this capture.
capture_status_stop_waiting: Stop requested; waiting for the daemon to finish.
network_empty_disconnected: Daemon not connected — network mapping unavailable.
network_empty_unsupported: Network mapping is not supported on this platform.
network_scan_controls_copy: Choose a detected network or enter a range manually.
network_ranges_hint: Select one · or leave blank for all
network_empty_no_devices: No devices discovered — run a scan to populate the map.
network_watch_dialog_intro_configure: Choose how often Antiwire should check this device. You will be notified whenever its connection state changes.
network_watch_dialog_intro_remove: Periodic presence checks and connection-change notifications will stop for this device.
analytics_empty_disconnected: Daemon not connected — analytics data unavailable.
analytics_empty_no_hosts: No remote hosts recorded in the last session.
analytics_geo_missing_hint: No country data in saved connections — enable GeoIP in Settings to locate new connections.
alerts_empty_none: No alerts in the feed yet.
ai_decisions_verdict_block_desc: Antiwire blocked this domain because a category set to Block met its confidence threshold.
ai_decisions_verdict_record_desc: A category met its confidence threshold and was recorded, but the domain was not blocked.
ai_decisions_verdict_clean_desc: No enabled category met its confidence threshold.
ai_decisions_empty_none: No AI decisions yet. Domains appear here once TypeSafe classifies them.
ai_decisions_empty_none_detail: Turn on AI classification in Settings to start classifying domains.
ai_decisions_empty_disconnected: Daemon not connected — AI decisions unavailable.
ai_decisions_delete_body: This removes the saved classification for {domain} from Antiwire. The next lookup can classify it again.
ai_decisions_advanced_body: This reads the official registration record for {domain} and classifies it again with that record. A newly registered name on hold can change the saved decision. Nothing runs until you confirm.
dashboard_stat_bars_download_aria: Download rate over the last minute
dashboard_stat_bars_upload_aria: Upload rate over the last minute
dashboard_stat_bars_connections_aria: Active connections over the last minute
dashboard_stat_bars_blocked_aria: Blocked connections per hour, last 12 hours
dashboard_top_apps_empty: No application traffic in the last 24 hours.
dashboard_active_empty: No applications are connected right now.
dashboard_active_unavailable: This daemon can’t attribute live connections to applications.
dashboard_active_new_aria: Opened a connection in the last minute
dashboard_collector_fallback: The collector cannot record traffic volume, so sent and received byte counts are unavailable.
error_page_body: This view failed to render. Navigation and the Antiwire service are still running.
error_fatal_body: The current view could not be shown. You can retry, go back to the dashboard, or reload the app.
settings_appearance_intro: Your language, your colors, your way. Changes apply immediately on this device.
settings_notifications_intro: Choose which connections and security events deserve your attention.
settings_activity_intro: Control location insights, stored activity, and how rules behave offline.
settings_dns_intro: Choose how domain names are resolved and which protections run on your network.
settings_network_intro: Manage automatic discovery of devices on your local network.
settings_forwarding_intro: Send security events to your monitoring tools and choose what to share.
settings_pending_desc: Save to apply changes across your settings.
settings_invalid_desc: Review invalid fields in DNS, Activity & storage, or Event Forwarding before saving.
settings_load_failed: Settings could not be loaded. Try connecting again.
records_quick_filters_desc: Every value in the selected range
records_quick_window_aria: Time range for services, countries, and destinations
records_time_filter_desc: Choose a day or narrow it to an hour
records_time_invalid: End time must be after start time
